why: The Dash were created by the Dynamo in 2013 with the Dynamo's orange and black colours and share Shell Energy Stadium and ownership; Dynamo supporters' groups such as The Surge explicitly support the Dash too.

Racing Louisville was founded by LouCity's ownership and shares Lynn Family Stadium; The Coopers supporters' group represents and leads support for both clubs from the Estopinal End, and the clubs run a joint '502 Crew' supporter-section programme.
Men's and women's teams of the same club: same ownership, same Inter&Co Stadium, and The Wall supporters' section (The Ruckus, Iron Lion Firm) backs both teams.

Both play at Providence Park; the Thorns' Rose City Riveters were founded by Timbers Army members and both groups sit under the 107 Independent Supporters Trust. Ownership of the two clubs has been separate since the 2024 sale of the Thorns, but the supporter base remains shared.

The Royals were relaunched in 2024 by Real Salt Lake's owners, are run within the RSL organisation and play at America First Field ('the RioT'); supporters' groups such as Los Caballeros Reales back both teams. Name and colours differ, so the identity is only partly shared.
Ultras-level friendship (Wilde Horde and The Unity) since Köln's 2011 win over Leverkusen handed Dortmund the title; listed among current Bundesliga fan friendships.
Milan's Curva Sud lists Sevilla among its current international twinnings (from around 2014), alongside CSKA Sofia and Partizan.
Herri Norte Taldea and Indar Gorri are twinned in the Basque left-nationalist ultras network.
Although the clubs contest the Basque derby, Herri Norte Taldea and Real Sociedad's ultras (Bultzada / Real Sociedad Firm) are twinned in the same Basque ultras network.
Herri Norte Taldea and Alavés's Iraultza 1921 are twinned in the Basque left-nationalist ultras network.
Herri Norte Taldea is twinned with Celtarras, Celta's left-wing, pro-independence ultras.
New friendship officially listed by Schalke's ultras in 2025 after reciprocal visits, built on shared dislike of Köln and Dortmund.
Ultras twinning since a chance meeting on a train in January 2000; renewed with mass visits to Bergamo in 2016 and 2022 and one of the best-known cross-border gemellaggi.
Twinning since about 1969-73, rooted in Fiorentina's closeness to Torino after Superga and a shared rivalry with Juventus; still active.
Juventude Leonina and Directivo Ultras XXI are twinned with Fiorentina ultras; Juve Leo wore black at the 2018 Lisbon derby to honour a murdered Fiorentina fan.
Historic twinning born in memory of Gigi Meroni; strained in 2009 and partly repaired in 2012; Genoa's most valued gemellaggio.
Genoa supporters are twinned with Marseille's South Winners only (Marseille's Commando Ultra is instead twinned with Sampdoria).
One of Italy's most solid ultras twinnings (Boys San / Curva Nord Inter and Lazio's Curva Nord), dating from the late 1980s; both far-right-leaning curve.
Official twinning since 2013; Nice ultras regularly appear at San Siro and sided with Inter ultras in the December 2018 clashes with Napoli.
Twinning with PSV's Ehv-Hools and Boys '91 made official in 2022-23.
Irriducibili and Ultras Sur twinned in 2001 ('divided by teams, united by mentality'), reinforced in 2007-08. Ultras Sur have been barred from the Bernabéu since 2014.
Twinning between the Irriducibili and Espanyol's Brigadas Blanquiazules, both far-right, built on shared hostility to Barcelona; the Spanish banner often appears in Lazio's Curva Nord.
Lille's Dogues Virage Est and Nice's Brigade Sud have been friends since the late 1990s; Lille shared its section with Nice ultras after the Brigade Sud was dissolved.

Both clubs' supporters sing You'll Never Walk Alone as their anthem; at the 2016 Europa League tie on the Hillsborough anniversary the two crowds sang it together, which won both sets of fans the FIFA Fan Award.
Feyenoord adopted You'll Never Walk Alone (Lee Towers' 1976 version) as a club anthem; Feyenoord's travelling fans sang it in tribute to Arne Slot when he moved to Liverpool.
Mainz 05 sing You'll Never Walk Alone before home matches (one of only two German clubs, with Dortmund); the link is often highlighted through Jurgen Klopp, who managed both clubs.

A long-standing fan friendship dating from the 1973, 1977 and 1978 European meetings, strengthened when Gladbach fans raised money for Hillsborough families; supporters still visit each other's grounds.
Lyon's Bad Gones declare a friendship with Real Madrid's Ultras Sur, who attended the Bad Gones' 35th anniversary match in 2022.
Commando Ultra '84 and AEK's Original 21 have been friends for about 35 years (with Livorno, the 'triangle of brotherhood'); AEK's 1989 visit shaped Marseille's ultras.
Napoli's curve are twinned with Dortmund ultras, a link brokered via Catania; Dortmund ultras urged fans to respect the friendship when travelling to Naples.
Listed as a Napoli twinning; Napoli ultras invited Feyenoord's hard core to Naples in 2023.
Twinning since 2017 between Napoli's Curva B (Ultras 1972) and PSG's K-Soce Team (Collectif Ultras Paris), with banners shown at each other's grounds.
Indar Gorri (Osasuna) and Bukaneros (Rayo) are twinned.
Indar Gorri (Osasuna) and Riazor Blues (Deportivo) are twinned.

Section 8 Chicago and the Timbers Army have had a friendship since about 2004, with members visiting each other's matches, joint trips such as the 2009 'Allied Invasion' of Seattle, and supporters' matches between the groups; Section 8 was a model for the 107IST.
Ultras Sur and Espanyol's Brigadas Blanquiazules have had a strong far-right alliance since 1988.
Official twinning between Roma's curva and Frente Atlético.
Biris Norte are listed as twinned with Marseille's Commando Ultra '84, within the left-wing ultras network.
Biris Norte and Riazor Blues, both left-wing, are officially twinned and display banners together when the teams meet.
Biris Norte are twinned with Rayo's Bukaneros in the left-wing ultras network.

Sections of both fan bases share a friendship that began when Wearside shipbuilders worked in Rotterdam in the 1970s and 80s; a 'Feyenoord Mackems' branch travels to the Stadium of Light with its own flag.
After the 1985 League Cup final, where Sunderland fans applauded Norwich's lap of honour and the fans swapped scarves, the clubs have played for a 'Friendship Trophy' whenever they meet.
Union's Hammerhearts and Gladbach's Sottocultura ultras have had an official group friendship since 2018 (contacts since 2009); the groups describe it as a group rather than club-wide friendship.
Lazio's ultras count West Ham among their main international friendships, which grew from fan contacts and the shared love of Paolo Di Canio; supporters attend each other's matches.
Informal friendship between AEK and Fenerbahçe fans, rooted in AEK's Constantinople origins ('Same City's Sons' banner, 2017).
The only two Bundesliga crowds that sing You'll Never Walk Alone before kick-off; in March 2016 both sets of fans sang it together after a Dortmund supporter died at the match.
Lazio fans previously had a strong twinning with Chelsea supporters, which cooled as the West Ham tie grew; still listed on some twinning maps.

The Spirit play at D.C. United's Audi Field and the Rose Room Collective is a supporters' group for both clubs; ownership and main supporters' groups (Spirit Squadron, Barra Brava/District Ultras) are separate.
Riazor Blues and Bukaneros keep good relations, short of a formal twinning.
A 37-year twinning (1982-2019) that Napoli's ultras ended in April 2019; some sources report a rapprochement since 2024.
Friendship with the Kop dating from 2010, when Inter's curva hosted Liverpool fans; Italian Wikipedia says it is not a true twinning.
Friendly relations between the fans grew after the 1965 European Cup quarter-final decided by a coin toss; German Wikipedia says only a few friendship scarves remain of it.
Supras Auteuil (PSG) and Köln's Wilde Horde 96 twinned in 2003; the German group still marks anniversaries although Supras dissolved.
Roma supporters have a friendship (not a formal twinning) with Udinese supporters.
Since 2024 the Sounders co-own and operate the Reign and both play at Lumen Field, but the Reign keep their own name, colours and supporters' groups (Royal Guard) separate from the Sounders' ECS.
Some Union fans have kept a friendship with Schalke fans since the 2001 DFB-Pokal final; not carried by the whole fan scene.
Both crowds sing You'll Never Walk Alone as their anthem (Celtic since the 1960s); Kevin's own example of the link (2026-09-28). Added in the 2026-10-09 rebuild.
Both sing You'll Never Walk Alone; the 2016-17 Champions League meetings were marked by the shared anthem. Added 2026-10-09.
